name: linux-arm64-kvm-guest-memory-v1
purpose: Run the ignored KVM guest-memory result checker across every exact ARM64 and generic KVM C command context, compare the sole finding with the complete candidate fixed source, and execute a controlled before/fixed ARM64 KVM selftest.

artifact_identity.raw_artifact_policy: The raw report, per-file logs, generated kernels, binaries, and initramfs were retained only for validation and are not repository artifacts.

finding.diagnostic: ignored kvm_write_guest_lock() failure in kvm_init_stolen_time may be hidden by successful return __retres
finding.source_behavior: The function returns the configured stolen-time IPA even when KVM could not initialize the 16-byte guest structure at that address.
finding.disposition: runtime-confirmed low-severity guest-visible false-success candidate; maintainer confirmation pending

complete_source_differential.source_change: Return INVALID_GPA when kvm_write_guest_lock() cannot initialize the stolen-time structure.

runtime_confirmation.guest_kvm: all CPUs started at EL2; KVM VHE mode initialized successfully
runtime_confirmation.control: The focused selftest binary, init, initramfs, QEMU command, machine, CPU, memory, and kernel configuration were identical; only the vulnerable versus fixed kernel source differed.

checker_policy.calls: direct calls to recognized kvm read/write guest-memory helpers with no result destination
checker_policy.function_scope: non-void definitions in the typed AST
checker_policy.successful_return: a value propagated from the same simple guest-address variable passed as the helper's second argument, or zero for a signed non-boolean integer return protocol
checker_policy.flow: forward CFG analysis with per-call pending state and direct local assignment propagation
checker_policy.deduplication: at most one diagnostic per ignored call
checker_policy.composite_addresses: not treated as one of their component variables

positive: ignored locked write followed by returning the guest address
ignored write followed by returning zero
silent: ignored call confined to an error-return path
returning one component of a composite guest address
a zero local embedded in a nonzero expression

candidate_disposition.status: automated exact-source finding with vulnerable-fail/fixed-pass ARM64 KVM runtime confirmation; maintainer confirmation pending
candidate_disposition.confirmation_scope: runtime confirmed under QEMU TCG, not maintainer confirmed or upstream accepted

limitations: The checker recognizes direct helper names only; wrappers, indirect calls, assigned-but-unchecked results, and values copied before the transfer are outside its inference.
CFG joins do not preserve relational branch predicates, and opaque callees can invalidate address-taken locals without being modeled.
A zero or address-valued return is only a candidate success protocol until the API and caller are reviewed.
The deterministic reproducer removes a memslot under userspace control before first vCPU entry; this demonstrates false success but not a guest-to-host security boundary violation.

The PV-time ABI text expects the structure to remain present in reserved guest memory, so maintainer review must decide whether post-configuration memslot deletion is within the supported VMM contract.
The runtime control uses QEMU TCG rather than physical ARM64 hardware.
Linux KVM maintainer review and upstream acceptance remain pending.
interpretation: The checker isolates one direct ignored guest-memory failure across all 83 exact KVM command contexts. The PV_TIME_ST contract promises an initialized structure address or NOT_SUPPORTED; the controlled memslot removal forces the write failure, the baseline kernel nevertheless returns the stale IPA, and the two-line fix changes the same execution to NOT_SUPPORTED while preserving the complete steal-time selftest. This establishes the implementation behavior but not whether the provoking VMM sequence is supported by the ABI.
